Note::integers¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

std::span<const std::int64_t> Note::integers() const

Borrow The Int64 Storage Without Conversion¶

integers() returns a read-only span over an Int64 Note’s native contiguous lanes. It is intended for host algorithms, range-based loops, bulk I/O, and foreign kernels that consume signed 64-bit integers. No allocation or copy is performed, and values are not parsed from text or converted from Float64.

Measurements such as lengths_chars(), count_substring(), and regex().count() return Int64 Notes, so their results can move through Note shape operations before this explicit host boundary is taken. Use int_item() only for a one-element result; integers() accepts any rank and cardinality.

Linear Order And Views¶

The returned span lists lanes in row-major logical order. Rank and extents are not embedded in std::span; query them from the Note. A row or slab returned by matrix() or slabs() can expose a smaller span into the same backing buffer without copying. Such a Note view owns a reference to that buffer and can outlive the source Note.

The bare span remains non-owning. Keep its Note alive, and do not retain the span beyond that lifetime. Use host when independent ownership is required.

integers() rejects every non-Int64 dtype and rejects undefined handles. A defined zero-element Int64 Note returns an empty span.

Example 1: Traverse A Measurement Result¶

const auto counts = pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::int64_t>{2, 5});
const auto lanes = counts.integers();
std::cout << '[';
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < lanes.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << lanes[i];
std::cout << "] size=" << lanes.size() << '\n';

Output¶

[2, 5] size=2

Example 2: Preserve Shape Beside The Flat Span¶

const auto grid = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::int64_t>{1, 2, 3, 4},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 2});
const auto lanes = grid.integers();
std::cout << '[';
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < lanes.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << lanes[i];
std::cout << "] shape=[" << grid.size(0) << ", " << grid.size(1) << "]\n";

Output¶

[1, 2, 3, 4] shape=[2, 2]

Example 3: A Note Row View Keeps Shared Storage Alive¶

pluss::Note row = pluss::Note::undefined();
{
  const auto matrix = pluss::note::make(
      std::vector<std::int64_t>{10, 11, 12, 20, 21, 22},
      std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 3});
  row = matrix.matrix()[1];
}

const auto lanes = row.integers();
std::cout << '[';
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < lanes.size(); ++i)
  std::cout << (i ? ", " : "") << lanes[i];
std::cout << "] retained-after-source\n";

Output¶

[20, 21, 22] retained-after-source

The row Note owns a shared reference. If only lanes had escaped the scope, accessing it would be invalid.

Example 4: Dtype Mismatch Is Not An Implicit Cast¶

try {
  (void)pluss::note::make(std::vector<bool>{true, false}).integers();
} catch (const pluss::Error& error) {
  const std::string message(error.what());
  std::cout << message.substr(0, message.find('\n')) << '\n';
}

Output¶

Note storage does not contain Int64 lanes

Example 5: Undefined Has No Integer Buffer¶

try {
  (void)pluss::Note::undefined().integers();
} catch (const pluss::Error& error) {
  const std::string message(error.what());
  std::cout << message.substr(0, message.find('\n')) << '\n';
}

Output¶

Note::integers() on undefined Note
